decisions.body:
Option 3: the plan is amended. Commit eb586f85 on this task branch rewrites D6 of extract-agent-round-runner after a decision review; read D6, FR7, NFR-R1, NG7 and tasks 2.3–2.3b before continuing.

What is decided:
- The Claude settings schema accepts exactly the four legacy keys: allowedTools, disallowedTools, maxTurns, roundTimeout. There are no keys for the startup-read and silence bounds; both stay the factory's (ProgramBounds).
- roundTimeout is the overall bound of every round and judge vote of the stage or check that declares it; the factory's overall bound applies when it is absent. No factory ceiling over it (NG7).
- Task 2.3 is ticked: the schema you built is the intended one.

What your question missed: the runner from task 1.2 takes all three bounds from ProgramBounds (AgentRound.java:127-132) and never reads roundTimeout. Its only round-time readers are ExecutorRoundExecution and JudgeRoundExecution, which tasks 4.1 and 5.1 delete. Left as is, every agent round would be killed at 30 minutes.

Continue with:
- 2.3a — RoundBounds, the one resolution of a round's bounds, wired into every consumer the task names, with the old-way sweep, RoundBoundsOwnerSpec and RoundBoundIdentitySpec. It must land before 4.1.
- 2.3b — measure the CLI's liveness cadence for a long tool call inside a subagent and on the Linux CLI. It must land before 5.1. A gap above 60 s is a blocker under spec-mismatch.md, never a raised constant.
- Then the remaining tasks in order.

This question is settled; do not raise the three bounds again.

decisions.body:
Other. The plan is amended on this task branch (commit d9e457dc). Read D4, D9, FR9, NFR-R2, NG8, NG9 and tasks 2.5, 2.5a, 5.1, 5.3, 7.2 before continuing.

(1) Task 2.5, continuation. D4 is rewritten after a decision review: a decision is continued from the branch record, never from the worker. The Claude session is worker-local state — a file on one machine, or in a box that is disposed before the decision commit — so there is no session resume.
- Task 2.5 now removes the resume half you built: `--resume` rendering, the refusal recognition, the fresh-start fallback, GF192, `AgentDialect.resumeRefused` and `continuation`, `ContinuationKey`, `resumable` in the Claude describe, with their specs. Keep only this: the runner writes a decision-request answer with no continuation key.
- Do 2.5 first. `checkSpecContract` is red on two dangling markers (`ClaudeDialectContinuationSpec`, `AgentRoundContinuationSpec`) until it lands; the task text names them.
- Task 2.5a is new: the decision records the question and options it answers, and the briefing renders them with the reply. It must land before 4.2 and 5.1.
- Do not build an engine path for the continuation key. That is NG8, deferred with its pickup condition. No ledger token `continued session=<prefix>` exists any more.

(2) Task 2.3b, Linux cadence. The human measures it and records the numbers in D6. Leave 2.3b unticked and do not measure it yourself. The macOS numbers are already in D6. Do not start 5.1 until 2.3b is ticked; if you reach 5.1 first, stop and report that 2.3b is still open.

Continue in order: 2.5, 2.5a, 2.6, then sections 3 and 4. Both questions are settled; do not raise session continuation again.

decisions.body:
Other. The plan is amended on this task branch; read D2, D12, D13, FR4, FR13–FR15, NG10, NG11
and sections 4–5 of tasks.md before continuing.

Your finding was right, and the cause is in the plan: task 4.1 switched the judge onto a
registry entry that did not exist. None of A, B or C is taken.

What is decided:
- Judge votes are removed. A judge check is one verdict request; `votes`, JudgeVoting and the
  majority rule are deleted. Several opinions are several judge checks in the verify list.
- No default judge. A judge check declares the same `executor:` block a stage declares, parsed
  and validated by the same owner. A missing block or model is a load error.
- `type: agent-cli` resolves to one registry entry under the reserved built-in name `claude`,
  with a stage half and a check half. No temporary fixed name.
- A judge check runs as a check round on the existing check path, in a fresh box of its own.
- The guard probe gets one owner. Today CheckRound does not probe, so a program verdict check
  in a fresh box is judged unprobed. Fix this first.

Work sections 4 and 5 in the order written in tasks.md, not by number:
4.0, 4.0a, 4.2, then 4.1, 4.3, 5.1, 5.1a, 5.2, 5.3.

2.3b: tasks 4.0, 4.0a and 4.2 do not wait for it. Task 4.1 and everything after it do. The
human measures the Linux half. If you reach 4.1 while 2.3b is open, stop and report that. The
silence bound for judge requests is D6 as written; do not raise it again.

Do not edit .gnomish/: this repository's own stage manifests keep the old judge form (NG11).

Task 2.3b closed, do 2.3c before 4.1

decisions.body:
Other. The plan is amended on this task branch (commit 0ee4e89b); read D14, D15, D3, D7, D8, D9,
FR18–FR22, NFR-R5, NG12, NG13 and section 5 of tasks.md before continuing.

Both findings were right, and both causes are in the plan.

Blocker A — none of the deletions you refused is asked for any more.
- The round source stays the one owner of a round's open and close for every entry.
  HostRoundEnvironmentSource and SandboxRoundEnvironmentSource are not deleted. The check
  acquisition stays provisioning only. This is your option A.
- New in 5.1: one port contract spec of RoundEnvironmentSource in :test-fixtures, run against
  every implementation, and Round.readDecision leaves the port unless you find a reader.
- 5.2 keeps the collapse of the round-token minting in adapters/git; the host/sandbox markers
  stay, reworded.

Blocker B — neither fallback option is taken.
- The raw-text question is retired. An agent's transform answer that is not a valid answer is
  failed/quality with one finding: one attempt burned, no repair round of the factory's own.
  Verdict and decision keep cannot-verify. No result event, a kill on a bound, a dead process
  stay failed/infrastructure. A program executor is unchanged.
- One read of the answer file, live and at recovery. DecisionRequestRead and its fallbacks are
  deleted (5.4). SnapshotTipCheck reads as the live round does.
- minItems stays 2. Do not build a channel beside the contract's Answer.
- The seven red Container*Spec features are fixed in 5.5; none is deleted or weakened.

5.0 is measured and ticked (D15, the table of 2026-11-23): the schema-enforced answer held on
macOS and Linux for both roles. Order: 5.1, 5.1a, 5.2, 5.4, 5.5, 5.6, 5.7, then 5.3.

Do not edit .claude/ or .gnomish/. Where a task names a row of manual-sync-pairs.md, list it in
implement.md under "Open (for the human)" and tick the task without it.

Both questions are settled; do not raise the round sources or the raw-text fallback again.

decisions.body:
Other. The plan is amended on this task branch; read D11 (the amendment of 2026-11-25 and the
   kill-window table), D14, D8 row "The round's continuation", FR10, FR11, NFR-R3, NG14, NG15 and
   section 6 of tasks.md before continuing.

   Your finding was right, and the cause is in the plan: D11 and D14 had no poll phase. Neither A
   nor B is taken as written.

   What is decided:
   - A poll is its own operation on the port: StageExecutor.poll beside execute; Request.pending()
     is removed. No branch on a flag.
   - The round source holds the open round. A poll opens nothing, mints nothing, closes nothing and
     writes nothing on the branch; a rotated key is the one write.
   - Going pending is not a close: one pending-round snapshot, on the start's result only.
   - The closing snapshot sits on the round's last registered commit and is judged from it, with
     the state.json lag settled. Your option A would have reported the factory's own commits as a
     boundary violation on the host.
   - Resume: the cell is restored at the run's assembly, before the engine chooses start or poll.
   - New window K5: closing snapshot registered, no closing commit — re-verified, never polled.

   Work in this order: 6.4a, 6.4b, 6.4c, 6.4d, then 6.5 and on. 6.4a comes first and must be shown
   red on the code as it stands; report what fails on each medium. 6.4b changes the port and
   nothing else.

   Not in scope: a client token on start (NG14), a retention window (NG15), cancel (NG6).

report.question:
Task 7.2 of extract-agent-round-runner (packaged-jar e2e through the Claude dialect) is blocked on NFR-O1: the ledger/round line must show `executor=claude@<version>`, and it shows `executor=agent-cli, protocolVersion=-`. Done this round: 6.5-6.9a and 7.1 ticked and verified (implement.md); 7.2 written (ClaudeRoundJarE2eSpec): the FR9 fresh-round-from-decision feature and the FR20 invalid-answer feature are green on macOS and Linux; only the NFR-O1 feature is under @PendingFeature (F1). 6.9a rule texts and other .claude/ edits are under 'Open (for the human)' in implement.md.

Cause (verified): DescribedExecutors.executorOf (domain/.../engine/DescribedExecutors.java:84-89) names an executor block without `name` by its type word (Participants.typeWord -> 'agent-cli'), while dispatch resolves the same block to the registry entry `claude` (StageDefinition.Executor#registryName(), ExecutorDispatch.java:76, VerifyCheck.java:180). Versions come only from the program describe preflight (DescribeOutcome.java:55-69), so ClaudeEntry.VERSION ('built-in') never reaches the engine. Same class elsewhere: usage participant names written to state.json (RoundExecution.java:149), the pending ask's name (TransformRound.java:73), check ledger lines with no version (RoundOutcomeLedgerWriter.java:87-88). Safe sites: ExecutorVersionCheck.compare compares only names present on both sides; ranBy pins only a named block, so adding built-ins changes no pin. D12 names a judge's participant by the entry it resolved to (design.md:620) but decides nothing for a stage's participant or for built-in versions. Alternative zero (leave agent-cli, no version) breaks the NFR-O1 promise; failure class of every option is a wrong-but-visible name, no stall or lost duty.

What I would do: A. One owner: executorOf names a block by registryName(), and DescribedExecutors carries the describe versions of every registry entry including built-ins (claude@built-in, command), CheckOutcome takes versions from the same place. Cost: the usage participant of an agent stage changes from 'agent-cli' to 'claude' (old attempt records keep 'agent-cli', so one task's totals may split across two names after an upgrade), ~100 test references. This is a decision on D12/D13 naming, so it needs /architect Mode C and /opsx:update before I build it.

Note also: tasks 7.3a and 7.3b are marked (human) paid-smoke runs; the stage's first check fails while any task is unticked, so the stage cannot pass until they are ticked.
options: A: name every participant by its registry entry and carry built-in describe versions (amend D12/D13, then I implement it in 7.2)
B: name by registry entry only, no version; the @<version> half deferred to externalize-claude-executor (NG1)
